nodes.summary: For `0 < n`, a symmetric nonnegative matrix has a positive vector `d` with `diag(d) A diag(d)` doubly stochastic if and only if it has total support.
nodes.title: Csima–Datta theorem

nodes.summary: A symmetric nonnegative matrix with total support has a positive vector `d` with `diag(d) A diag(d)` doubly stochastic.
nodes.title: Csima–Datta: sufficiency of total support

nodes.summary: Let $n \ge 1$ and let $A$ be a real $n \times n$ matrix all of whose entries are strictly positive. Then there are vectors $r, c \in \mathbb{R}^n$ with strictly positive entries such that the matrix with entries $r_i A_{ij} c_j$ is doubly stochastic, that is, its entries are nonnegative and each of its rows and each of its columns sums to $1$.
nodes.title: Sinkhorn's scaling theorem
